chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu al-Maghra Humayd ibn al-Muthanna al-Ajali, who said: Abu Hanifa, a man from our companions, narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying:
The one who knows the dispute (or difference/divergence), he is not a weakened individual.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), a central figure in Shia hadith.
key_terms.الِخْتِلَاف: Dispute, difference, or divergence; often refers to distinguishing between truth and falsehood or understanding differing opinions.
key_terms.مُسْتَضْعَف: Weak, vulnerable, or easily deceived; one who lacks the strength to discern or stand firm.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'not weakened' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to define the spiritual resilience of the faithful, where 'al-ikhtilaf' specifically refers to discerning the distinct characteristics of truth from falsehood amidst the multiplicity of sects. This knowledge protects the believer from being 'mustad'af' (weak or easily misled) by false claims, a concept central to Shia epistemology regarding the recognition of the Imams and the authenticity of their teachings.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hussain ibn Abi’l-Khattab, from Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Abu’l-Maghra, Hameed bin Muthanna al-‘Ajali, that he said: I was told by Abu Hanifa, a man from our companions, of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The one who knows the dispute, he is not a weakened individual.
